login.hero:
Send one stream.
Go live everywhere.
login.heroText: Ingest over SRT or RTMP and distribute to YouTube, Facebook, Twitch and your own servers, each in the right bitrate.
login.title: Sign in
login.subtitle: Access the {{name}} control console

dashboard.emptyText: A stream gives you an ingest address and stream key for OBS, vMix or a hardware encoder. Then add the platforms to send it to.
dashboard.mediaDisabledText: This is a development or test setup without MediaMTX and FFmpeg. On a server installed with the installer, ingest and outputs work automatically.

settings.redirectUri: Redirect URI for the app registration

updates.subtitle: Restream updates itself from GitHub. Production follows the main branch, test follows the test branch.

why.dns: The server address does not exist. Check the server URL of this destination.
why.refused: The server refused the connection. Check the server URL and port.

streams.title: Streams & keys
streams.subtitle: Each stream has its own ingest address and secret stream key. Send it once from your encoder; Restream distributes it.
streams.nameHint: A stream key is generated for you. You can add destinations next.
streams.obsHint: In OBS: Settings → Stream → Service "Custom…", paste the server and the stream key.
streams.srtHint: For SRT encoders (OBS, vMix, hardware): the stream key is in the streamid. Use caller mode.
streams.rotateHint: The old key stops working immediately and a connected encoder is disconnected.
streams.confirmRotate: Generate a new stream key? The current key stops working and a connected encoder is disconnected.
streams.playbackHint: Anyone with these links can watch the incoming stream, e.g. on your own website. Turn off to make them return 404. The links don't contain the stream key.
streams.confirmDisable: Disable this stream? The encoder is disconnected and new connections are refused.
streams.confirmDelete: Delete {{name}} and all its destinations? This cannot be undone.
streams.detailsHint: Used as title and description when Restream creates a broadcast on a connected account (YouTube, Facebook, Twitch) on Go live. Events have their own title.
streams.recordingHint: Recordings are MP4 files on this server; you find them under Recordings. You can always start one with the Record button on the dashboard.
streams.autoRecord: Record automatically on Go live (stops with Stop all)

destinations.title: Destinations
destinations.subtitle: Where each stream goes. Go live starts every destination that is included; you can also start and stop them one by one on the dashboard.
destinations.rtmpServerHint: rtmp:// or rtmps:// address of the server, without the stream key.
destinations.srtServerHint: srt://host:port of the receiving server (caller mode).
destinations.keyKeep: Stored: {{masked}}. Leave empty to keep it.
destinations.ytKeyHint: YouTube Studio → Go live → Stream → Stream key.
destinations.fbKeyHint: Facebook Live Producer → Streaming software → Stream key. Facebook needs RTMPS.
destinations.passphraseHint: 10 to 79 characters, only if the receiver requires encryption.
destinations.passphraseKeep: A passphrase is stored. Leave empty to keep it.
destinations.includedLong: Include in Go live (start together with the stream)
destinations.passthroughHint: Sends the incoming stream unchanged: best quality, almost no CPU. The bitrate is what your encoder sends, so set a keyframe interval of 2 seconds there.
destinations.transcodeHint: Re-encodes for this destination with its own bitrate, resolution and frame rate (H.264 + AAC at a constant bitrate, with the keyframe interval the platform asks for). Uses about 1 to 2 CPU cores per 1080p output.
destinations.accountMissing: Connected account missing — choose another one
destinations.withKeyHint: Paste the stream key from the platform's studio. Works for every platform and account.
destinations.withAccountHint: Restream creates the broadcast itself on Go live, with the stream's title, and ends it on Stop. Scheduled events are announced on the platform.
destinations.noAccounts: No {{platform}} account connected yet — connect one under Accounts
destinations.about_instagram: Instagram: needs a professional (Business or Creator) account. In Instagram Live Producer you get a new server URL and stream key for every broadcast, so paste both here before you go live. Instagram shows portrait video (9:16, 720p, 30 fps), which is what this preset sends.
destinations.about_kick: Kick: copy the stream URL and stream key from Kick › Settings › Stream. Kick takes H.264 up to 1080p60 and 8 Mbps.
destinations.about_x: X: in Media Studio › Producer, create a source and copy its RTMPS URL and stream key; the source keeps them, so you do this once. Start the broadcast in Producer once Restream sends video. X takes 720p30 up to 4 Mbps; keyframes every 3 seconds are set for you. Easier: connect the X account under Accounts and Restream does all of this.
destinations.about_linkedin: LinkedIn: live streaming needs approval by LinkedIn. Create a live event with "Custom stream (RTMP)", then copy the stream URL and key (available about an hour before the start). LinkedIn takes up to 1080p30 and 6 Mbps.
destinations.serverFromPlatform: Copy the server or stream URL from {{platform}}.
destinations.igKeyHint: Instagram Live Producer → Stream key. It changes for every broadcast.
destinations.xKeyHint: Media Studio → Producer → Sources → your source → Stream key.
destinations.liKeyHint: LinkedIn live event → Stream setup → Stream key.
destinations.landscapeHint: The picture keeps the shape of your ingest.
destinations.portraitHint: Restream cuts the middle 9:16 out of the picture, for platforms that show portrait video such as Instagram. Keep the important part in the centre of the shot.
destinations.transcodeAdvised: {{platform}} takes at most {{height}}p at {{fps}} fps. Passthrough only works when your encoder already sends that; otherwise choose Transcode.
destinations.withAccountHintX: Restream creates a source on the X account once. On Go live it publishes the broadcast with the stream's title as soon as X receives the video (X announces it in a post) and ends it on Stop. Events are not announced on X.

mail.title: Mail server
mail.subtitle: Restream sends notifications and test messages through your own SMTP server.
mail.security_starttls_hint: Recommended. Connects on port 587 and requires the upgrade to TLS 1.2 or newer; the connection fails rather than falling back to plain text.
mail.security_tls_hint: Encrypted from the first byte, usually on port 465.
mail.security_none_hint: No encryption. Only for a relay on this server or your own network (port 25).
mail.passwordSet: A password is stored. Leave empty to keep it.
mail.verifyHint: Test connection checks the saved settings: it connects, starts TLS and signs in without sending a message.
mail.saveFirst: Switch mail on and save a server and sender address first.
mail.dkimText: DKIM signs every message so receiving servers can check it really comes from your domain. Generate a key, publish the DNS record at your domain, then switch signing on.
mail.dkimNoKey: No key yet. Generate one to see the DNS record.
mail.dkimRegenerateConfirm: Generate a new DKIM key? Mail fails DKIM checks until you replace the DNS record.
mail.recipientsHint: One address per line, for example a NOC mailbox. Up to 20.
mail.notifyNeedsMail: Notifications are only sent once the mail server is switched on and saved.
mail.event_streamDown_hint: The encoder stopped for more than 20 seconds while destinations were live, and when it is back.
mail.event_outputFailed_hint: A platform refuses or drops the stream three times in a row, and when it is live again.
mail.event_mediaServerDown_hint: MediaMTX has not answered for a minute, and when it runs again.
mail.event_backupFailed_hint: A scheduled or manual backup did not complete.
mail.event_backupSucceeded_hint: A report after every successful backup.
mail.event_updateFinished_hint: After an update from the console, including a rollback.
mail.event_updateAvailable_hint: Checked every six hours on your current channel.
mail.subject: Subject

backups.title: Backups
backups.subtitle: Encrypted full and incremental backups of the database, configuration and recordings to your own server over SCP, FTPS or FTP, with restore from that location.
backups.notConfigured: Backups are not set up yet. Enter a location and an encryption passphrase below, then use Test connection.
backups.notConfiguredShort: Set up a location and a passphrase first.
backups.protocol_scp_hint: Recommended. File transfer over SSH with a key that Restream generates; the server's host key is pinned at the first connection.
backups.protocol_ftps_hint: FTP with explicit TLS (AUTH TLS) on port 21. The connection fails if the server does not support TLS.
backups.protocol_ftps-implicit_hint: FTP over TLS from the first byte, usually port 990, for older servers.
backups.protocol_ftp_hint: Plain FTP. Only for a server in your own network.
backups.ftpWarning: Plain FTP sends the login unencrypted. The backup files themselves are always encrypted, but prefer SCP or FTPS.
backups.passwordSet: A password is stored. Leave empty to keep it.
backups.pathHint: Relative to the login directory, or an absolute path starting with /. Created when missing.
backups.keyRegenerateConfirm: Generate a new key? Replace the public key on the backup server afterwards.
backups.keyHint: Add this public key to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys of the backup user on the server.
backups.keyNone: No key yet. Generate one, or use a password.
backups.hostKeyForgetConfirm: Forget the pinned host key? Only do this when you know the server was reinstalled.
backups.testOk: Connected, wrote and removed a test file.
backups.encryptionText: Every backup is encrypted with AES-256-GCM before it leaves this server. The key comes from your passphrase. Without the passphrase a backup cannot be restored, also not by us.
backups.passphraseHint: At least 12 characters. Store it in your password manager: you need it to restore onto a new server.
backups.passphraseChangeWarning: Older backups keep the old passphrase. After a change the next backup is a full one.
backups.keepChainsHint: Each with its incrementals. Older ones are removed from the location.
backups.summary: {{full}}; {{incremental}}. The last {{keep}} full backups are kept.
backups.summary_daily: A full backup every day at {{time}}
backups.summary_monthly: A full backup on the 1st of every month at {{time}}
backups.summaryIncr_daily: an incremental backup on the other days
backups.none: No backups on this location yet.
backups.deleteConfirm: Delete this full backup and its incrementals ({{n}} in total) from the location?
backups.safetyDumps: {{n}} safety copy(ies) of the database from before a restore are kept on the server in /var/lib/restream/backups/pre-restore.
backups.restoreChain: Restores the full backup plus {{n}} incremental backup(s) up to this one.
backups.restoreWhat1: The database (users, streams, destinations, settings) and recordings are replaced by the backup. Live outputs stop.
backups.restoreWhat2: The backup location stays as configured here. Secrets are re-encrypted when the backup comes from another server.
backups.restoreWhat3: A copy of the current database is saved on this server first.
backups.restoreWhat4: Everyone is signed out and signs in with the accounts from the backup.
backups.signedOutText: The restore signed everyone out. Sign in with an account from the backup; the result is under Backups › Activity.

embed.title: Embed on a website
embed.subtitle: A player in your own style that you place on any website with one line of code. Choose who may play the stream; this also applies to the HLS and WebRTC links above.

mode.token: Only with a link I hand out

modeHint.public: The player and the links work everywhere.
modeHint.domains: The player only works when it is embedded on the websites you list. Direct links only play from those sites.
modeHint.token: Every player and link needs a signed link from this page. Links can expire and you can revoke all of them at once.

embed.domainsHint: One per line. *.example.com also covers example.com and every subdomain.
embed.linksHintToken: Create a link for each website or person. Anyone with the link can watch until it expires.
embed.linksHintDomains: Optional: a signed link also plays outside your websites, for example in a TV app or VLC.
embed.confirmRevoke: Revoke all links of this stream? Players that use one stop within a minute, also on websites.
embed.codeHint: Paste this code into your website. The player scales with the page and switches to full screen.
embed.autoplayHint: Browsers only start video automatically without sound; viewers can switch the sound on.
embed.needLink: Create a signed link first; the embed code uses it.

accounts.title: Connected accounts
accounts.subtitle: Connect YouTube channels, Facebook pages, Twitch channels and X accounts once. Destinations can then go live without copying stream keys, and events are announced on the platforms.
accounts.publicUrlMissing: Set the public URL of this server first; the platforms send you back to it after signing in.
accounts.appMissing: An administrator first sets up the app for this platform (see the setup guide).
accounts.reconnect: Access expired or revoked — connect again
accounts.confirmRemove: Remove {{name}}? Destinations that use it stop working until you choose another account or a stream key.

what.youtube: Creates the live broadcast on Go live, schedules events with their own watch link, and ends the broadcast on Stop.
what.facebook: Every page you manage is added. Goes live on the page and schedules events as upcoming live videos.
what.twitch: Gets the stream key itself and sets the stream title. Events go into the stream schedule (Affiliates and Partners).
what.x: Creates a stream source on the account once, publishes the broadcast on Go live (with an announcing post) and ends it on Stop. Events are not announced on X.

accounts.appsText: Each platform needs an app that you register once in its developer console. The guide walks you through it and gives every value to copy; the secret is stored encrypted.
accounts.secretKeep: Leave empty to keep the stored secret.
accounts.reconnectForChat: Connect again to show the comments of this page in the live chat.
accounts.askAdmin: {{platform}} is not set up yet. Ask an administrator to follow the setup guide on this page.

how.title: Connect a channel in three steps
how.text: Restream works like other apps that post for you: you click Connect, a pop-up from the platform asks you to sign in and to allow Restream to go live on your behalf, and the channel appears here. Steps 1 and 2 are done once.
how.step1Text: The platform sends the pop-up back to this address after signing in.
how.step1Done: Set. The platforms send the pop-up back to this server.
how.step2Text: A short, guided registration in the developer console of the platform. Click a platform to open its guide.
how.step3Text: Sign in in the pop-up and click Allow. The pop-up closes and the channel or page appears below, ready for destinations and events.

popup.waitingText: A pop-up from the platform is open. Sign in there and allow access; this page updates by itself.

youtube: Choose the Google account that owns the channel. Is the channel on a Brand Account? Choose the Brand Account in the list.
Does Google say it hasn't verified the app? That is your own app: click Advanced › Go to … (unsafe).
Google asks if the app may manage your YouTube account. Click Continue (or Allow).
The pop-up closes and the channel appears on this page.
facebook: Sign in to Facebook, or click Continue as … .
Choose the pages Restream may use. Select every page you want to stream to.
Check the permissions (publish videos, manage posts, read comments) and click Save or Continue.
The pop-up closes and every chosen page appears on this page.
twitch: Sign in to Twitch with the account of the channel.
Twitch asks if the app may read the stream key and manage the broadcast and schedule. Click Authorize.
The pop-up closes and the channel appears on this page.
x: Sign in to X with the account you want to go live on.
X asks if the app may read your profile and manage your live broadcasts. Click Authorize app.
The pop-up closes and the account appears on this page.

require.youtube: The channel needs live streaming enabled (YouTube Studio › Go live). The first time, YouTube can take up to 24 hours to enable it.
require.facebook: Facebook only allows live video through apps on pages with at least 100 followers, managed by an account that is at least 60 days old.
require.twitch: Scheduling events needs Affiliate or Partner status; going live works for every channel.
require.x: X only lets paid accounts (X Premium) that are not protected go live from streaming software. Connecting works without it, but going live is refused.

youtube.title: {{app}} wants access to your Google Account

facebook.title: {{app}} is requesting access to your pages
items: Create and manage content on your pages
Read content and comments on your pages
Show a list of the pages you manage

x.title: {{app}} wants to access your X account
items: See your profile and posts you can see
Create and manage your live broadcasts
Stay connected until you revoke access

guideIntro.youtube: You register Restream as an app in Google Cloud. It is free and takes about 10 minutes. Afterwards everyone with operator rights can connect channels with the familiar Google pop-up.
guideIntro.facebook: You register Restream as an app at Meta for Developers. It is free and takes about 10 minutes. Afterwards pages are connected with the familiar Facebook pop-up.
guideIntro.twitch: You register Restream as an application in the Twitch developer console. It takes about 5 minutes.
guideIntro.x: You register Restream as an app in the X Developer Console. It takes about 10 minutes. X bills API use per call with prepaid credits; going live takes only a handful of calls per broadcast.

youtube.title: Create a Google Cloud project
youtube.text: Sign in with the Google account that will manage the app (it doesn't have to own the channel) and create a project, for example “Restream”.

youtube.title: Enable the YouTube Data API v3
youtube.text: Check that your new project is selected at the top of the page and click Enable.

youtube.title: Branding: the name in the pop-up
youtube.text: Google Auth Platform › Branding (click Get started the first time). Enter the app name people will see in the pop-up, a support email, and under Authorized domains this domain:

youtube.title: Audience: External and published
youtube.text: Choose External. Then click Publish app.
youtube.note: In Testing mode only the test users you add can connect, and Google ends the connection after 7 days. Published without Google's verification works for your own channels; the pop-up then shows a warning you click through (Advanced › Go to …).

youtube.title: Data access: the YouTube permission
youtube.text: Click Add or remove scopes, paste this scope under Manually add scopes (it is shown as “Manage your YouTube account”), click Add to table, Update and Save:

youtube.title: Create the OAuth client
youtube.text: Clients › Create client › Application type Web application. Add these two values and click Create:
youtube.note: Copy the client secret right away: Google only shows it once. Lost it? Add a new secret to the client.

facebook.title: Create the app
facebook.text: Meta for Developers › Create app. Enter the name people will see in the pop-up, choose the use case “Authenticate and request data from users with Facebook Login”, and connect your business portfolio when asked (or skip that step).

facebook.title: Add the page permissions
facebook.text: Use cases › Authenticate and request data… › Customize › Permissions. Add each of these permissions:

facebook.title: Allow the redirect
facebook.text: Same use case › Settings: keep Client OAuth login and Web OAuth login on, and add this under Valid OAuth Redirect URIs. Save.

facebook.title: App domain and privacy policy
facebook.text: App settings › Basic: add this domain under App domains, fill in a privacy policy URL and choose a category. Save.

facebook.title: Who can connect
facebook.text: In Development mode only people with a role on the app can connect. Add your technicians under App roles › Roles (Administrator, Developer or Tester); they accept the invitation on Facebook.
facebook.note: To publish to everyone, switch the app to Live. Meta then asks for Business verification and App Review of these permissions. Test in Development mode first.

facebook.title: Copy App ID and App secret
facebook.text: App settings › Basic: copy the App ID, and click Show next to App secret.

twitch.title: Register the application
twitch.text: Twitch developer console › Register your application. Twitch requires two-factor authentication on your account for this. Enter the name people will see in the pop-up.

twitch.title: Redirect URL
twitch.text: Add this under OAuth Redirect URLs:

twitch.title: Category and client type
twitch.text: Category Broadcaster Suite, client type Confidential. Click Create.

twitch.title: Copy Client ID and secret
twitch.text: Applications › Manage: copy the Client ID and click New Secret.

x.title: Create the app
x.text: Sign in to the X Developer Console with an X account (it doesn't have to be the account you stream on) and click Create App. Enter the name people will see in the pop-up.

x.title: Turn on user authentication
x.text: App › User authentication settings › Set up. Choose OAuth 2.0, type of app Web App (confidential client), and add these two values as Callback URI and Website URL:
x.note: The callback URI must match exactly, including https and without a trailing slash.

x.title: Permissions
x.text: Restream asks for these permissions in the pop-up itself; you don't have to tick them in the console:

x.title: Add API credit
x.text: X API use is pay-per-use. If the console asks for it, add a small amount of credit under Billing; without credit X refuses the calls.

x.title: Copy the Client ID and Client Secret
x.text: App › Keys and tokens › OAuth 2.0 Client ID and Client Secret.
x.note: X shows the client secret only once. Lost it? Regenerate it and paste the new one here.

accounts.tryTitle: Try it: connect your first account
accounts.tryText: Click the button. The platform's pop-up opens; sign in and allow access. Does that work? Then setup is done.
accounts.tryAfterSave: Save the values first; then the connect button appears here.

x.title: Paid X account required
x.text: X only lets paid accounts (X Premium, or a verified organisation) go live from streaming software. Without it X refuses the broadcast and the dashboard says so. Protected (private) accounts cannot go live either.

events.title: Events
events.subtitle: Plan broadcasts ahead. Restream announces them on the connected platforms, goes live at the start time and stops at the end.
events.emptyText: Plan a live event: viewers find it on YouTube, Facebook and Twitch beforehand, and Restream goes live on time.
events.confirmStart: Start {{title}} now? Its destinations go live.
events.confirmCancel: Cancel {{title}}? It is removed from the platforms.
events.destinationsHint: Destinations on a connected account are announced on the platform right away. The others simply go live at the start.
events.autoStart: Go live automatically at the start

recordings.title: Recordings
recordings.subtitle: Every broadcast you record, as an MP4 file on this server. Watch it in the browser or download it.
recordings.retentionHint: Older recordings are deleted automatically. Backups include the recordings.
recordings.emptyText: Press Record on the dashboard during a broadcast, or switch on automatic recording for a stream or event.
recordings.confirmDelete: Delete the recording {{name}}? The file is removed from the server.
recordings.titleHint: Also used as the file name of the download.

live.offAir: Viewer counts appear here as soon as a destination is on air.
live.noStatsHint: Viewer counts and chat are read from destinations that use a connected account. Destinations with a typed stream key only send video.
live.chatOffAir: The chat of YouTube, Facebook and Twitch appears here while you are on air.

chat.title: Combined chat
chat.subtitle: Messages from YouTube, Facebook and Twitch in one window, for the stream that is on air.
chat.readOnly: Restream shows the chat; replying and moderating is done on the platforms themselves. The chat is kept with the broadcast under Analytics.

analytics.title: Analytics
analytics.subtitle: Every broadcast with its duration, peak and average viewers, and the chat afterwards.
analytics.emptyText: A broadcast is recorded here automatically from the moment the first destination goes live until you stop.
analytics.noSamples: Not enough viewer counts yet for a graph.
analytics.noChat: No chat messages in this broadcast.
analytics.chatTruncated: Showing the first 1,000 messages; the CSV export has all of them.
analytics.confirmDelete: Delete this broadcast with its statistics and chat? Recordings are kept.

failover.backupHint: A second stream key for a backup encoder or a second connection. When the main feed drops, the live destinations switch to the backup feed by themselves (a reconnect of a second or two). Once the main feed has been stable for {{seconds}} seconds, Restream switches back.
failover.backupKeyHint: Same RTMP server as the main feed ({{server}}), with this key.
failover.confirmRemove: Remove the backup key? A backup encoder that is connected now is disconnected.
failover.confirmRotate: Make a new backup key? The backup encoder needs the new key.
failover.switchBack: Switch back to the main feed after
failover.switchBackHint: How long the main feed must run without interruption before Restream leaves the backup feed. 0 switches back at once.
failover.fallbackHint: When no feed comes in while destinations are live, Restream sends this image with silence, so the platforms keep the broadcast open. It starts only after a feed was on air, and stops as soon as a feed is back.
failover.imageHint: PNG or JPEG, 16:9 (1920×1080 works best), up to 8 MB.
failover.maxMinutesHint: After this time the destinations stop sending and wait for a feed, so a broadcast does not stay on the image all night.
failover.onBackupText: The main feed dropped; the destinations carry the backup feed. Restream switches back once the main feed has been stable for {{seconds}} seconds.
failover.onFallbackText: No feed comes in. The destinations show the fallback image until an encoder reconnects.
failover.expiredText: No feed came back within {{minutes}} minutes. The destinations are waiting for an encoder; press Stop all to end the broadcast.

integrations.title: API & webhooks
integrations.subtitle: Connect Restream to your other projects: they control it with an API key and hear what happens through webhooks.
integrations.keysIntro: Send the key as "Authorization: Bearer rsk_…". A key works like a user with its role (never more than the person who made it), and every change it makes is in the audit log with its name. Keys cannot sign in, manage users or keys, or restore backups.
integrations.confirmRevoke: Revoke API key {{name}}? Projects that use it stop working right away.
integrations.keyOnce: Copy the key now: Restream only stores a fingerprint and cannot show it again.
integrations.keyNameHint: Which project uses it, so you know what breaks when you revoke it.
integrations.roleHint_viewer: Read only: streams, status, events, statistics.
integrations.roleHint_operator: Also go live, stop, record and manage streams, destinations and events.
integrations.roleHint_admin: Everything an administrator can do, except the actions keys never get.
integrations.webhooksIntro: Restream POSTs a signed JSON message to your URL when something happens, such as a stream going live or switching to its backup feed. Failed deliveries are retried after 30 s, 2 min, 10 min, 30 min, 2 h and 6 h.
integrations.allEventsLong: Send all events (also ones added in later versions)
integrations.secretHint: Used to sign every message (header X-Restream-Signature). Keep it in the receiving project.
integrations.confirmRotateSecret: Make a new signing secret? The receiver rejects messages until it has the new secret.
integrations.urlHint: https:// is strongly advised. Addresses on this server itself are refused.
integrations.verifyText: Every message carries X-Restream-Signature: t=<unix time>,v1=<HMAC-SHA256 of "t.body" with the signing secret>. Check it on the raw body and refuse messages older than five minutes. X-Restream-Event-Id is the same for a retry, so you can ignore duplicates.
integrations.ev_stream_ingest_started: An encoder started sending (main or backup feed)
integrations.ev_stream_source_changed: The destinations switched feed: main, backup, fallback image or none
integrations.ev_output_reconnecting: A destination lost its connection and is reconnecting
integrations.ev_broadcast_ended: A broadcast ended, with its viewer figures
